name: Anabolic steroids for voice

lead: Anabolic steroids and testosterone can lower the voice because they masculinize the larynx. Some people in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles seek this deeper voice.

Androgens act on the androgen receptor, including in laryngeal tissue, thickening and lengthening the vocal folds in the way male puberty does. Medical sources list voice deepening as a virilizing side effect, not an indication, and no trials test steroids as a voice treatment. A French-language article on synthetic anabolic steroids and the voice dates to 1964.

paras: Medical sources describe voice change as occurring gradually alongside other virilizing effects during androgen exposure. Published material on using steroids specifically for voice is sparse.

Documented risks include irreversible virilization in women, acne, hair loss, fertility suppression, lipid and liver effects, and legal restrictions as controlled substances. Voice changes in women may be permanent.

angle.text: Androgens, including anabolic steroids, thicken and lengthen the vocal folds and lower the voice, and some people seek this effect. It is a documented side effect of virilization rather than a studied use, and some changes may be permanent.

lead: Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) are synthetic androgens that, like testosterone, can lower the voice by acting on the larynx. Voice deepening is listed among the virilizing effects of testosterone and its esters, and in women it is reported as a possible effect of androgens [1][2][3][4]. For people chasing a more masculine presentation, a deeper voice is part of the overall impression of a commanding, mature physique, and some in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles view androgens as a route to it.

Medical sources describe voice deepening as a side effect of treatment, not an indication, and note that androgen-related masculinization in women can be irreversible [3][4]. Testosterone therapy in transgender men is described as producing a deeper pitch, listed among the irreversible changes, with the larynx growing more prominent as in male puberty [5].
Published material directly on using steroids to change the voice is sparse. A 1964 French-language article on synthetic anabolic steroids and the voice exists in the literature [6].
infobox: Described as irreversible in women and children [4]
Schedule III (US), Schedule IV (Canada), Class C (UK) [4]

paras: The long-acting ester testosterone cypionate lists deepening of the voice among its virilizing effects, alongside acne and increased body and facial hair [1]. Testosterone more broadly can cause voice deepening in women [2]. Oxandrolone's article describes voice deepening among masculinizing effects in women and states some masculinizing changes can be irreversible [3]. Wikipedia's anabolic steroid article lists irreversible voice deepening among female-specific effects and as a masculinizing effect in women and children [4].

Adult male vocal folds are longer than female ones, which is associated with lower male pitch [7]. In describing testosterone therapy for transgender men, Wikipedia says that at puberty the larynx bones and cartilage grow less in females than in males, and that testosterone leads to deeper pitch and a more prominent larynx [5].

On T Nation, a news excerpt posted in a thread about law-enforcement operations against steroid laboratories lists a deepening of the voice among reported side effects of anabolic steroids, along with body hair growth [8]. In another thread, a woman describing a self-directed steroid course reported a scratchy throat that she thought might be the start of voice virilization, and said she decided to stop [9].

Androgens carry other documented risks, including acne, hair loss, suppressed sperm production, effects on blood lipids and the liver (particularly oral 17-alkylated agents), and use is contraindicated in pregnancy [1][2][3]. Wikipedia reviews describe links between steroid use and aggression, hypomania and depression in some studies [4]. AAS are controlled substances in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom [1][4].
No studies found of anabolic steroids used for voice goals. Related literature on androgen effects on the voice exists, including a 1964 article on synthetic anabolic steroids and the voice [6].

lore.intro: Voice change appears in steroid forums mainly as a side-effect warning, particularly in discussions among women, rather than as a goal.

timeline.event: Testosterone is discovered and synthesised, and anabolic steroids begin to be used medically [4].
A French-language article on synthetic anabolic steroids and the voice is published [6].
